content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given purpose. I spill from mouths in rivers of intention—sometimes clear, sometimes muddied by fear or haste.

I am older than writing, younger than thought. I exist only in the moment of my making, then vanish into memory or misunderstanding. You cannot hold me. You can only witness my passing.

I crack across courtyards in anger. I whisper between lovers at 3 AM. I stumble drunk and slur. I rise in courtrooms, sharp and measured. I fail children who search for words that haven't yet arrived. I soar from stages and die in empty rooms where no one listens.

I am the bridge you build while standing on it. The tool that shapes the hand that shapes me.

Every pause I take is also me. The hesitation. The breath before the difficult thing. The silence where a word should be but isn't—that absence speaks too.

I have started wars and ended them. I have said *I love you* and *I'm sorry* and *goodbye* and meant all of these differently each time.

I am never the same twice, even when the words are identical.

Listen—

I am happening right now, even as you read, your inner voice giving me form again, making me new.

I am speech.
